Run the pollution-to-health pipeline and report it

Source: R/pollution.R
vrfpol.Rd

Resolves the exposure (synthetic demo data, a CSV with an exposure column and an optional income column, a NAPS-style pull with a value column and a unit, or scalar arguments), logs the assumptions, and when they all hold runs the concentration-response, attributable-fraction, displaced-mortality, burden and equity stages. polrpttxt() renders the result as plain text. It is the one-call version of the pollution functions, made for scripts and the command line: it never stops with an R error for bad input, but returns a report whose status says what went wrong.

Usage

vrfpol(
  poll,
  y = "allcause",
  reg = NULL,
  years = NULL,
  demo = FALSE,
  expcsv = NULL,
  expomean = NULL,
  expoprev = NULL,
  ref = NULL,
  brate = 500,
  basrateper = 1e+05,
  pop = 1e+06,
  rare = FALSE,
  hirate = FALSE
)

polrpttxt(report)

Arguments

poll

"no2" or "pm25" (also "PM2.5"), in either case.

y

Outcome key for the concentration-response function; the mortality outcomes count deaths, "chiast" incident cases.

reg, years

Labels for the report.

demo

Use synthetic demo data (TRUE or FALSE).

expcsv

Path of a CSV with an exposure column in micrograms per cubic metre, or a NAPS pull with a value column and a unit column (required with value): each row is converted by its own unit, NO2 in ppb at 1.88 micrograms per cubic metre per ppb (the WHO 2021 conversion at 25 C and 1 atm), and any other unit is an error. With a CSV or the demo data the exposed are the rows above ref: expoprev is their share and expomean their mean, so Levin's formula is not diluted twice.

expomean, expoprev

Scalar inputs used when neither demo nor expcsv is given: the mean exposure among the exposed and the share of the population exposed. A wrapper must never default one of them to zero: a prevalence of zero silently zeroes the burden, which is why the two are required together.

ref

Counterfactual reference concentration; NULL takes the pollutant's default (PM2.5 5.8, NO2 10; see crfpm25).

brate

Baseline outcome rate per 100,000 per year (unlike polbrdn, which takes a rate per person-year).

basrateper

The denominator brate is quoted per: 100,000 (the default), or 1 for a rate per person-year such as a crude death rate of 0.012.

pop

Population at risk (persons).

rare

TRUE when the outcome really is rarer than one case per 100,000 per year. Without it a rate that converts to less than that is an assumption failure, because it is also what a rate per person-year passed as per 100,000 looks like (0.008 per person-year is 800 per 100,000; as 0.008 per 100,000 the burden is 100,000 times too small). The check is on the converted rate, so it holds whatever basrateper is.

hirate

TRUE when the outcome really is more common than 10,000 per 100,000 a year (no population's all-cause death rate is); without it such a rate is an assumption failure.

report

A result of vrfpol() (or a list with the same parts); anything else is refused with an R error.

Value

vrfpol(): the report as a list of class rmbl_pollution_report (plot() draws it); its status is "ok", "assumption_failure" or "error", and the attribute exitstat carries a command-line exit code (0, 1 or 2). An argument the pipeline cannot use (no exposure data at all, a vector where a single number is expected, an unknown outcome, a missing reference, a directory as expcsv) is an "error" report with exit status 2, never a raw R error; an exposure at or below the reference is a valid run with zero attributable cases, and the scalar inputs expomean and expoprev go together (one without the other is an error report). On "ok" the report also holds inputs (the resolved exposure mean and prevalence, the rate per 100,000, the population, the reference and the rows dropped), assumptions (a list of assumption, ok, note) and pipeline (crf, paf, pafci, displaced, burden and equity, which is NULL without income data). polrpttxt(): a single character string with embedded newlines, ending in a STATUS: line (or "ERROR:" and the message for an error report).

Details

The assumption log checks that the exposure mean is finite and non-negative and at most 10,000 micrograms per cubic metre, the prevalence is in \([0, 1]\), the baseline rate (converted to per 100,000) is zero or between 1 and 10,000 per 100,000 a year (from 1e-6 with rare, up to 100,000 with hirate), the population is positive and at most 10 billion, the reference is finite and non-negative, and the pollutant has a CRF. Any failure gives status "assumption_failure" and skips the stages.

With data (a CSV or the demo), the "exposed" are the rows above the reference: their mean is expomean and their share expoprev. Empty cells and missing-value tokens (NA, n/a, null, - ...) are dropped with a message; text that is not a number (a detection-limit flag such as "<2") and negative values stop the run with an error report. A gzip, bzip2 or xz file is decompressed; UTF-16 and Latin-1 files are decoded. An income column, when present and numeric, gives the equity stage (expconcidx).

The stages: crfpm25 or crfno2; attrfrac with the CRF's interval; mortdisp for removing the excess exposure over the exposed population, with \(\beta = \log(RR) / (\bar x - x_{ref})\); and polbrdn. The demo data are 1,000 synthetic units with lognormal exposures at the scale of Toronto NO2 or PM2.5 levels and five income groups, drawn with a fixed seed (R's own random stream is restored).

See also

polbrdn and the other stage functions to run one step on its own.

Examples

r <- vrfpol("no2", demo = TRUE)
r$status
#> [1] "ok"
r$pipeline$paf
#> [1] 0.02733115
cat(polrpttxt(r))
#> ==================================================================
#>   verify-pollution -- NO2 -> allcause
#>   data:   demo (synthetic)
#> ==================================================================
#> 
#> Inputs
#>   exposure mean:      24.261
#>   exposure prevalence:0.981
#>   baseline rate/100k: 500.00
#>   population:         1,000,000
#>   reference conc:     10
#> 
#> Assumption log
#>   [PASS] exposure finite and non-negative -- mean 24.26113743 vs ref 10
#>   [PASS] exposure within the concentration-response range (at most 10,000 ug/m3) -- exposure_mean=24.26114
#>   [PASS] prevalence in [0,1] -- exposure_prevalence=0.981
#>   [PASS] brate finite: zero, or between 1 and 10,000 per 100k -- brate=500 per 100k per year
#>   [PASS] population finite, positive and at most 10 billion -- population=1,000,000
#>   [PASS] reference finite and non-negative -- reference=10
#>   [PASS] pollutant supported by the CRFs -- Current CRFs: NO2 (log-linear), PM2.5 (log-linear all-cause; Burnett IER for IHD and stroke). Other pollutants reject.
#> 
#> Concentration-response
#>   RR:       1.0286
#>   source:   Huangfu & Atkinson (2020) Environ Int 144:105998; WHO (2021) Global AQ Guidelines
#> 
#> Attributable fraction (PAF): 0.0273  (95% CI 0.0138 to 0.0534, from the risk's limits)
#> 
#> Mortality displaced
#>   expected avoided deaths: 136.6
#> 
#> Burden of pollution
#>   attributable deaths:   136.7
#> 
#> Equity analysis
#>   concentration index: -0.0647
#> 
#> STATUS: ok

# Scalar inputs: a city of 2.8 million at a PM2.5 mean of 9.
s <- vrfpol("pm25", expomean = 9, expoprev = 1,
                      brate = 750, pop = 2.8e6, reg = "Toronto")
s$pipeline$burden$attrcases
#> [1] 510.8617
attr(s, "exitstat")
#> [1] 0

# A CSV of measurements with an income column.
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
utils::write.csv(data.frame(exposure = c(12, 18, 25, 31, 9), income = 1:5), f,
                 row.names = FALSE)
vrfpol("no2", expcsv = f)$pipeline$equity$concidx
#> [1] 0.02947368

# A rate per person-year passed as per 100,000 fails an assumption ...
bad <- vrfpol("no2", expomean = 20, expoprev = 1,
                        brate = 0.008)
bad$status
#> [1] "assumption_failure"
# ... and an argument it cannot use is an error report, not an R error.
vrfpol("no2")$error
#> [1] "no exposure data: pass expcsv, or expomean and expoprev, or demo = TRUE"
